findings.title: Title Screen Menu Low Contrast
findings.problem: The menu box has a dark background with light text and a thin cyan outline, but the overall contrast is low against the similarly dark, textured background. The 'New Driver' and 'Controls' options are hard to distinguish from the environment.
findings.why: Players may struggle to read or focus on the menu options at a glance, reducing immediate usability and making the game feel less polished.
findings.fix: Increase the menu box’s background opacity or add a subtle drop shadow to separate it from the background; use a brighter highlight color for the selected option.

findings.title: Arena Radar Missing Sweep and Contacts
findings.problem: The radar is a static black disc with no visible sweep line or contact indicators. It appears as a blank instrument rather than an active sensor.
findings.why: This breaks immersion and makes the UI feel broken or non-functional, undermining player trust in the HUD’s feedback system.
findings.fix: Add a rotating sweep line (e.g., animated teal arc) and small blips for detected entities (even if none exist yet) to simulate active scanning.

findings.title: City UI Overlap and Poor Hierarchy
findings.problem: The top banner contains multiple lines of dense text overlapping the environment, and the bottom-left vehicle status box blends into the cracked ground texture with no clear border or elevation.
findings.why: Critical information like location and vehicle status is hard to parse quickly, especially during fast navigation, reducing readability and visual clarity.
findings.fix: Reduce the top banner’s opacity or add a semi-transparent black mask behind the text; give the bottom-left status box a distinct border and slight lift (drop shadow) to separate it from the ground.

findings.title: Constructor Text Field No Visual Feedback
findings.problem: The 'Name' input field is a plain rectangle with no cursor, placeholder text, or active state indicator — it looks like a disabled or empty label.
findings.why: Players may not realize they can type here, leading to confusion about how to proceed with car creation, hurting onboarding.
findings.fix: Add a blinking cursor when focused and a placeholder text ('Enter car name') when empty; use a slightly brighter border or glow to indicate interactivity.

findings.title: Road HUD Top Bar Too Thin and Invisible
findings.problem: The progress bar at the top is extremely thin and lacks clear fill color or gradient, blending into the gray road background.
findings.why: Players may miss their mission progress or misjudge remaining distance, especially under motion blur or at speed, reducing situational awareness.
findings.fix: Thicken the bar to at least 10px height, use a high-contrast fill color (e.g., bright yellow or orange), and add a dark outer stroke to make it stand out from the road.
